diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $k \geq 1$ and let $\delta \in (0,\infty]$. Consider $\varepsilon$-fine Whitney sets $\{q_j^\pm\}_{j = 1}^\infty \subset \Omega^\pm$ for $\Omega^\pm_\delta$ with respect to $\gamma$.
so that $|b_j^+|^2 \simeq d(q_j^-)^{2k-1}m(B_j)$, where $B_j = B(q_j^-,\varepsilon d(q_j^-))$

issues.failure_explanation: The exterior case of the discretization estimate (\eqref{eq:discretization_estimate} with sources $q_j^-\in\Omega^-$) is declared 'analogous' to the interior case, but the key normalization step $|b_j|^2\simeq d(q_j)^{2k+1}$ is false for exterior points far from $\gamma$: for $|q|\to\infty$ one has $\int_\gamma|w-q|^{-2k-2}|dw|\simeq |\gamma|\,|q|^{-2k-2}$, so $|b_j^+|^2\simeq |q_j^-|^{2k+2}\simeq d(q_j^-)^{2k+2}$, one power more than claimed. Consequently the statement itself is false for $\delta=\infty$: a Whitney set for the unbounded set $\Omega^-$ contains infinitely many points with $|q_j^-|\to\infty$, and for these the $L_2$-normalized $\psi_j^+=b_j^+(w-q_j^-)^{-(k+1)}$ converge (up to a unimodular constant) uniformly on $\gamma$ to $|\gamma|^{-1/2}$, so for $f\equiv 1\in L_2^+(\gamma)$ one gets $|(f,\psi_j^+)|\to|\gamma|^{1/2}$ and $\sum_j|(f,\psi_j^+)|^2=\infty$; the upper frame bound fails. The same false comparability is used in the proof of Lemma removal (whose frame hypothesis, for a Whitney set of all of $\Omega^-$ with normalized wavelets, is therefore never satisfied), and the proof of the case $\delta<\infty$ is reduced to the false $\delta=\infty$ statement via that lemma, so the intended finite-$\delta$ theorem is left without proof.

failure_location.quote: We prove this estimate for the case of $\sum_{j=1}^\infty |b_j^- F^{(k)}(q^+_j)|^2$; the other case, where $+$ is replaced by $-$, and vice versa, is analogous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the $\delta=\infty$ case with weights $d(q_j)^{k+1/2}$ in place of $L_2$-normalization (the written computations in fact prove exactly this weighted discretization for both interior and exterior); prove Lemma removal for these weighted wavelets (its compactness argument goes through verbatim); then for $\delta<\infty$ observe that $d(q)^{2k+1}\simeq |b_j|^2$ uniformly for $d(q)\le\delta$, recovering the normalized frame statement for all finite $\delta$, and drop (or weaken) the normalized $\delta=\infty$ claim.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem lusin_frame is false as stated when $\delta=\infty$, and its proof for $\delta<\infty$ (the case used in the applications) rests on the false case and on Lemma removal, whose proof uses the same invalid estimate. Proposition frames_for_hardy_spaces (frame for $L_2^\pm(\gamma)$) inherits this for $\delta=\infty$ and lacks a valid proof for $\delta<\infty$ as written. The interior-source estimate and the square function estimates are unaffected.
issues.title: Lusin frame theorem fails for delta = infinity: L2-normalization of exterior wavelets is not comparable to d(q)^{2k+1} for far source points
issues.why_classification: The advertised finite-$\delta$ frame result survives with a contained rework (a change of normalization in the auxiliary $\delta=\infty$ case and in the removal lemma), but the $\delta=\infty$ statement must be weakened and the proof architecture for $\delta<\infty$ must be repaired; this is more than a local fix yet involves no new global machinery.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: G(z) = F(z) -q_0\sum_{n=1}^\infty \alpha_n z^{-n-1} + kq_0z^{k-1}\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\alpha_n}{n+k} z^{-n-k} = F(z) - q_0 \sum_{n=1}^\infty\alpha_n \frac{n}{n+k}z^{-n-1}

issues.failure_explanation: For $z\in\Omega^-$ the Cauchy integral of the boundary values of a function $H_-$ analytic in $\Omega^-$ and vanishing at infinity equals $-H_-(z)$ (this is the sign convention of Theorem hardy_splitting). The term $w^{k-1}\int_a^w\zeta^{-k-1}F\,d\zeta$ has exterior Laurent expansion $-\sum_n\frac{\alpha_n}{n+k}w^{-n-1}+c\,w^{k-1}$, so the Cauchy integral of $-kq_0$ times it is $-kq_0\sum\frac{\alpha_n}{n+k}z^{-n-1}$, not $+kq_0\sum\frac{\alpha_n}{n+k}z^{-n-1}$ as displayed. With the paper's $g$ one gets $G=F-q_0\sum\alpha_n\frac{n+2k}{n+k}z^{-n-1}$, and $G^{(k)}\neq(1-q_0z^{-1})F^{(k)}$. Concrete check: $k=1$, $F=z^{-1}$ (so $f=-w^{-1}$): the paper's $g$ yields $G=z^{-1}-\tfrac{3q_0}{2}z^{-2}$, $G'=-z^{-2}+3q_0z^{-3}$, whereas $(1-q_0/z)F'=-z^{-2}+q_0z^{-3}$. The correct definition is $g=(1-q_0w^{-1})f+kq_0w^{k-1}\int_a^w\zeta^{-k-1}F\,d\zeta$, for which the identity holds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign of the integral term in the definition of $g$ (to $+kq_0w^{k-1}\int_a^w\zeta^{-k-1}F\,d\zeta$) and correct the corresponding sign in the Laurent computation using that the exterior Cauchy integral of an exterior analytic decaying function is its negative; the rest of the argument is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the constructed $g$ does not satisfy $G^{(k)}(q_j)=0$, so the proof of part (i) of Proposition no_lusin_basis (and hence the non-basis conclusion for $L_2^+(\gamma)$ and its use in Lemma removal) is not established; the statement itself remains true.
issues.title: Sign error in the construction of g in the proof of Proposition no_lusin_basis (i)
issues.why_classification: A local sign correction in one definition and one display restores the argument; no conclusion, scope, or dependent result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: For a bi-Lipschitz map $\rho$ of $\R^n$ with constant $\mathcal{L}$, Lebesgue measure scales by at most $\mathcal{L}^{\pm n}$, not $\mathcal{L}^{\pm 1}$: e.g. $\rho(x)=x/\mathcal{L}$ has $\max(\mathrm{Lip}(\rho),\mathrm{Lip}(\rho^{-1}))=\mathcal{L}$ and $m(\rho(E))=\mathcal{L}^{-n}m(E)<\mathcal{L}^{-1}m(E)$ for $n\ge2$, $\mathcal{L}>1$. Hence the displayed inequality is false, and the stated bound $N\le 4^n\mathcal{L}^{3n+1}\sigma$ is not proved; the correct argument gives $N\le 4^n\mathcal{L}^{4n}\sigma$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\frac{1}{\mathcal{L}}$ by $\frac{1}{\mathcal{L}^n}$ in the measure estimate and restate the bound as $N\le 4^n\mathcal{L}^{4n}\sigma$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicit numerical value of the covering constant in the lemma is wrong; finiteness of $N$, and therefore the Whitney-set conclusion used for Example explicit_whitney_partition, is unaffected.
issues.title: Incorrect measure-scaling under bi-Lipschitz maps gives a false covering-constant bound
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of an exponent; no result depends on the specific constant.
